1	# Agent Skills
2	
3	A personal collection of [agent skills](https://agentskills.io/home) — both custom-authored and cherry-picked from upstream repos — installable as a single package.
4	
5	📚 **[Read the docs](https://daviddwlee84.github.io/agent-skills/)** for the full guide, conventions, and skill index.
6	
7	## Install
8	
9	<!-- snippet:install (keep in sync with docs/_snippets/install.md) -->
10	```bash
11	npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills
12	```
13	
14	> **Note**
15	> The trailing `/skills` matters. Without it, `npx skills` will look in
16	> `.agents/skills/` of the upstream repo, which contains a different
17	> layout. The `skills/` suffix points the installer at the
18	> `skills/local/` and `skills/vendor/` trees.
19	<!-- /snippet:install -->
20	
21	## What's in here
22	
23	- **`skills/local/`** — custom-authored skills.
24	  - [`project-knowledge-harness`](skills/local/project-knowledge-harness/) — TODO + backlog + pitfalls structure with init / kanban / promote / add-todo / sweep-inbox toolkit. ([docs](https://daviddwlee84.github.io/agent-skills/skills/project-knowledge-harness/))
25	  - [`quantatitive-factor-researcher`](skills/local/quantatitive-factor-researcher/) — Python quant-research persona. ([docs](https://daviddwlee84.github.io/agent-skills/skills/quantatitive-factor-researcher/))
26	  - [`skill-author`](skills/local/skill-author/) — Author new skills following [agentskills.io](https://agentskills.io/skill-creation/best-practices) best practices; ships `new-skill.sh` scaffolder and `lint-skill.sh` linter. ([docs](https://daviddwlee84.github.io/agent-skills/skills/skill-author/))
27	  - [`verifiable-surfaces`](skills/local/verifiable-surfaces/) — Design CLIs/tools/services with `--help`/`--dry-run`/`--print-config`/isolated-state smoke, and verify config/CLI/dotfile/IaC changes via app-native loaders before claiming done. ([docs](https://daviddwlee84.github.io/agent-skills/skills/verifiable-surfaces/))
28	  - [`mkdocs-site-bootstrap`](skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/) — Bootstrap a MkDocs Material site + GitHub Pages deploy; consent-gated via `.skills/preferences.yaml`; ongoing `add-docs-page.sh` helper. ([docs](https://daviddwlee84.github.io/agent-skills/skills/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/))
29	  - [`marimo-batch-mlflow`](skills/local/marimo-batch-mlflow/) — Opinionated fork of upstream `marimo-batch`: Tyro CLI (dataclass or Pydantic) + MLflow tracking + live `mlflow-widgets` chart, dual-mode (`mo.app_meta().mode == "script"`) UI/CLI from one notebook. ([docs](https://daviddwlee84.github.io/agent-skills/skills/marimo-batch-mlflow/))
30	  - [`dvc-ml-workflow`](skills/local/dvc-ml-workflow/) — DVC ([treeverse/dvc](https://github.com/treeverse/dvc)) pipelines + queued experiments with metrics auto-bound to ephemeral commits; ships `init-dvc-project.sh`, `queue-helper.sh` (with `grid` cartesian-product enqueue), `lint-dvcyaml.sh`. ([docs](https://daviddwlee84.github.io/agent-skills/skills/dvc-ml-workflow/))
31	  - [`mlflow-tracking`](skills/local/mlflow-tracking/) — Generic [MLflow](https://mlflow.org/docs/latest) skill: SQLite + `mlflow ui` for solo, vendored PostgreSQL + MinIO docker-compose stack for teams; covers LLM tracing, model registry (aliases), and autologging across all officially-supported frameworks. ([docs](https://daviddwlee84.github.io/agent-skills/skills/mlflow-tracking/))
32	  - [`agent-history-hygiene`](skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/) — Commit SpecStory chat transcripts + `.claude/plans/*.md` alongside feature diffs; bootstrap pre-commit + gitleaks + secret-redactor into new repos; enforce rotate-first, rewrite-last leak remediation (never reflexive `git push --force`). ([docs](https://daviddwlee84.github.io/agent-skills/skills/agent-history-hygiene/))
33	- **`skills/vendor/`** — third-party skills synced from upstream via [`vendor.yaml`](vendor.yaml). Do not edit these locally; `make sync` will clobber changes. Skills can be flat (`skills/vendor/<name>/`) or grouped into a **series** (`skills/vendor/<series>/<name>/`).
34	  - Flat:

36	    - [`streamlit-to-marimo`](skills/vendor/streamlit-to-marimo/) — from [marimo-team/skills](https://github.com/marimo-team/skills); convert Streamlit apps to marimo notebooks. ([docs](https://daviddwlee84.github.io/agent-skills/skills/streamlit-to-marimo/))
37	    - [`anywidget`](skills/vendor/anywidget/) (frontmatter name: `anywidget-generator`) — from [marimo-team/skills](https://github.com/marimo-team/skills); generate anywidget components for marimo notebooks. ([docs](https://daviddwlee84.github.io/agent-skills/skills/anywidget/))

Complements local [`skill-author`](skills/local/skill-author/). ([docs](https://daviddwlee84.github.io/agent-skills/skills/skill-creator/))

49	
50	## Categories in the install UI
51	
52	The grouped picker UI of `npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills`
53	is driven by [`skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`](skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json) —
54	seven plugin groupings (`skill-authoring`, `project-memory`,
55	`engineering-quality`, `ml-workflow`, `notebooks`, `fullstack-nextjs`,
56	`infra-and-docs`) covering all skills in
57	this repo. Anything not listed there falls under **Other** automatically.
58	
59	```bash
60	# Validate the manifest (paths exist, no duplicates, name not reserved,
61	# on-disk skills covered).
62	make marketplace
63	```
64	
65	The manifest lives under `skills/`, **not** at the repo root, because the
66	install command's `/skills` subpath makes the CLI read
67	`<repo>/skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`. See
68	[npx skills metadata model](https://daviddwlee84.github.io/agent-skills/reference/npx-skills-metadata/)
69	for the full mechanism, the `kebabToTitle` group naming rule, reserved
70	marketplace names, and the `marketplace.json` vs `plugin.json` distinction.
71	
72	## Repo memory
73	
74	This repo dogfoods `project-knowledge-harness` on itself:
75	
76	- [`TODO.md`](TODO.md) — priority/effort-tagged backlog.
77	- [`backlog/`](backlog/) — research notes for `P?` items (when populated).
78	- [`backlog/inbox.md`](backlog/) — quick-capture inbox; sweep into `TODO.md` later.
79	- [`pitfalls/`](pitfalls/) — symptom-grep-able knowledge base of past traps (when populated).
80	
81	```bash
82	# Validate TODO.md and render kanban-style board
83	make kanban
84	
85	# Quick add structured TODO entry
86	./scripts/add-todo.sh --priority P3 --effort M --title "..." --description "..."
87	
88	# Move an active TODO to ## Done in same commit as the implementation
89	./scripts/promote-todo.sh --title "<substring>" --summary "<shipped summary>"
90	
91	# Triage backlog/inbox.md interactively
92	./scripts/sweep-inbox.sh
93	```
94	
95	Full workflow: [Project memory](https://daviddwlee84.github.io/agent-skills/workflows/project-memory/).
96	
97	## Vendor system
98	
99	```bash
100	# Add a vendored skill (auto-syncs)
101	./scripts/add-vendor.sh owner/repo/path/to/skill
102	# or via Makefile
103	make add-vendor SOURCE=owner/repo/path/to/skill
104	
105	# Group into a series subdir (skills/vendor/<series>/<name>/)
106	./scripts/add-vendor.sh --series fullstack-nextjs vercel/vercel-plugin/skills/nextjs
107	
108	# Sync all vendored skills from upstream
109	make sync
110	
111	# Check for upstream updates (dry-run)
112	make sync-check
113	```
114	
115	Full workflow: [Adding vendor skills](https://daviddwlee84.github.io/agent-skills/workflows/adding-vendor-skills/).
116	
117	**Dependencies:** `gh` (GitHub CLI, authenticated) and `yq` (YAML processor).
118	
119	## Docs site
120	
121	The docs site is built with MkDocs Material + `mkdocs-llmstxt` + `mkdocs-copy-to-llm`.
122	
123	```bash
124	uv sync --extra docs
125	make docs-serve         # http://127.0.0.1:8000/
126	make docs-build         # produces ./site/
127	```
128	
129	Deployed automatically to GitHub Pages on push to `main` via [`.github/workflows/docs.yml`](.github/workflows/docs.yml).
130	
131	If you want to apply the same docs stack to your own project, see [Downstream docs stack recipe](https://daviddwlee84.github.io/agent-skills/reference/docs-stack-recipe/).
132	
133	## Adding a new local skill
134	
135	Use the bundled scaffolder (recommended — seeds the agentskills.io best-practice template):
136	
137	```bash
138	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh <skill-name>
139	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/lint-skill.sh skills/local/<skill-name>
140	```
141	
142	Or with the upstream init:
143	
144	```bash
145	cd skills/local
146	npx skills@latest init [skill-name]
147	```

1	# Karpathy's LLM Wiki pattern
2	
3	A reference summary of the **personal knowledge base maintained by an LLM**
4	pattern, as articulated by Andrej Karpathy in late 2025. This page is
5	documentation, not a skill — it captures the idea so we can decide later
6	whether to vendor an existing implementation (e.g. `obsidian-second-brain`)
7	or author a local skill of our own.
8	
9	## Sources
10	
11	- [`gist.github.com/karpathy/442a6bf555914893e9891c11519de94f`](https://gist.github.com/karpathy/442a6bf555914893e9891c11519de94f)
12	  — the long-form "LLM Wiki" pattern document, written to be copy-pasted
13	  into your own LLM agent so it can co-design the specifics with you.
14	- [`x.com/karpathy/status/2039805659525644595`](https://x.com/karpathy/status/2039805659525644595)
15	  — the original announcement tweet ("LLM Knowledge Bases"), which is
16	  the ~1-page version of the gist and the seed of the broader pattern.
17	
18	## TL;DR
19	
20	The wiki is a **persistent, compounding artifact**. RAG re-derives knowledge
21	from raw sources on every query; an LLM Wiki *compiles* that knowledge once
22	into structured markdown and *keeps it current* as new sources arrive.
23	
24	> Obsidian is the IDE; the LLM is the programmer; the wiki is the codebase.
25	> — Karpathy, [LLM Wiki gist](https://gist.github.com/karpathy/442a6bf555914893e9891c11519de94f)
26	
27	## The original tweet (verbatim)
28	
29	> **LLM Knowledge Bases**
30	>
31	> Something I'm finding very useful recently: using LLMs to build personal
32	> knowledge bases for various topics of research interest. In this way, a
33	> large fraction of my recent token throughput is going less into
34	> manipulating code, and more into manipulating knowledge (stored as
35	> markdown and images). The latest LLMs are quite good at it. So:
36	>
37	> **Data ingest:** I index source documents (articles, papers, repos,
38	> datasets, images, etc.) into a `raw/` directory, then I use an LLM to
39	> incrementally "compile" a wiki, which is just a collection of `.md` files
40	> in a directory structure. The wiki includes summaries of all the data in
41	> `raw/`, backlinks, and then it categorizes data into concepts, writes
42	> articles for them, and links them all. To convert web articles into `.md`
43	> files I like to use the Obsidian Web Clipper extension, and then I also
44	> use a hotkey to download all the related images to local so that my LLM
45	> can easily reference them.
46	>
47	> **IDE:** I use Obsidian as the IDE "frontend" where I can view the raw
48	> data, the compiled wiki, and the derived visualizations. Important to
49	> note that the LLM writes and maintains all of the data of the wiki, I
50	> rarely touch it directly. I've played with a few Obsidian plugins to
51	> render and view data in other ways (e.g. Marp for slides).
52	>
53	> **Q&A:** Where things get interesting is that once your wiki is big
54	> enough (e.g. mine on some recent research is ~100 articles and ~400K
55	> words), you can ask your LLM agent all kinds of complex questions
56	> against the wiki, and it will go off, research the answers, etc. I
57	> thought I had to reach for fancy RAG, but the LLM has been pretty good
58	> about auto-maintaining index files and brief summaries of all the
59	> documents and it reads all the important related data fairly easily at
60	> this ~small scale.
61	>
62	> **Output:** Instead of getting answers in text/terminal, I like to have
63	> it render markdown files for me, or slide shows (Marp format), or
64	> matplotlib images, all of which I then view again in Obsidian. You can
65	> imagine many other visual output formats depending on the query. Often,
66	> I end up "filing" the outputs back into the wiki to enhance it for
67	> further queries. So my own explorations and queries always "add up" in
68	> the knowledge base.
69	>
70	> **Linting:** I've run some LLM "health checks" over the wiki to e.g.
71	> find inconsistent data, impute missing data (with web searchers), find
72	> interesting connections for new article candidates, etc., to
73	> incrementally clean up the wiki and enhance its overall data integrity.
74	> The LLMs are quite good at suggesting further questions to ask and look
75	> into.
76	>
77	> **Extra tools:** I find myself developing additional tools to process
78	> the data, e.g. I vibe coded a small and naive search engine over the
79	> wiki, which I both use directly (in a web ui), but more often I want to
80	> hand it off to an LLM via CLI as a tool for larger queries.
81	>
82	> **Further explorations:** As the repo grows, the natural desire is to
83	> also think about synthetic data generation + finetuning to have your LLM
84	> "know" the data in its weights instead of just context windows.
85	>
86	> **TL;DR:** raw data from a given number of sources is collected, then
87	> compiled by an LLM into a `.md` wiki, then operated on by various CLIs
88	> by the LLM to do Q&A and to incrementally enhance the wiki, and all of
89	> it viewable in Obsidian. You rarely ever write or edit the wiki
90	> manually, it's the domain of the LLM. I think there is room here for an
91	> incredible new product instead of a hacky collection of scripts.
92	
93	## Architecture
94	
95	Three layers, from the gist:
96	
97	1. **Raw sources** — your curated source documents (articles, papers,
98	   images, datasets). **Immutable** — the LLM reads but never modifies
99	   them. This is your source of truth.
100	2. **The wiki** — a directory of LLM-generated markdown (summaries,
101	   entity pages, concept pages, comparisons, an overview, a synthesis).
102	   The LLM owns this layer entirely; you read it, the LLM writes it.
103	3. **The schema** — a `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` that tells the LLM how
104	   the wiki is structured, what the conventions are, and what workflows
105	   to follow. You and the LLM co-evolve this over time.
106	
107	## Operations
108	
109	| Operation | What it does |
110	| --------- | ------------ |
111	| **Ingest** | Drop a new source into `raw/`. The LLM reads it, summarizes, files it under the right entity/concept pages, updates the index, appends to the log. A single source might touch 10–15 pages. |
112	| **Query** | Ask a question. The LLM reads the index, drills into relevant pages, and answers — as markdown, a comparison table, a Marp deck, a matplotlib chart. **File the good answers back into the wiki** so explorations compound. |
113	| **Lint** | Periodic health check. Find contradictions, stale claims, orphan pages, missing cross-references, data gaps. Suggests new questions to investigate and new sources to look for. |
114	
115	## Two special files
116	
117	- **`index.md`** — content-oriented catalog. Every page listed with a link
118	  and one-line summary, organized by category. The LLM updates it on every
119	  ingest and reads it first when answering a query. At ~100 sources / a few
120	  hundred pages this works without embedding-based RAG.
121	- **`log.md`** — chronological, append-only. Use a consistent prefix
122	  (e.g. `## [2026-04-02] ingest | Article Title`) so the log becomes
123	  greppable: `grep "^## \[" log.md | tail -5`.
124	
125	## Why this works
126	
127	Maintenance — not reading or thinking — is what kills personal wikis.
128	Updating cross-references, keeping summaries current, noting contradictions
129	across dozens of pages: humans give up because the burden grows faster than
130	the value. LLMs don't get bored, don't forget a back-link, and can touch
131	15 files in one pass. The wiki stays maintained because the cost of
132	maintenance is near zero.
133	
134	The pattern is, in spirit, Vannevar Bush's [Memex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memex)
135	(1945) — a private, curated knowledge store with associative trails. The
136	part Bush couldn't solve was *who does the maintenance*. The LLM does.
137	
138	## Ecosystem
139	
140	Implementations and adjacent tools that have grown around this pattern:
141	
142	- **[`eugeniughelbur/obsidian-second-brain`](https://github.com/eugeniughelbur/obsidian-second-brain)**
143	  — a Claude Code skill (not an Obsidian plugin) that pushes the pattern
144	  further: 31 slash commands + scheduled agents + Python scripts. Adds
145	  AI-first conventions (machine-readable preambles, bi-temporal facts,
146	  a "Two-Output Rule" where every answer also updates relevant pages),
147	  vault-first research that scans existing notes before going to the
148	  web, and `_CLAUDE.md` / `index.md` / `log.md` / `SOUL.md` /
149	  `CRITICAL_FACTS.md` (≈120 tokens always loaded) at the vault root.
150	  *"If Karpathy's wiki is a knowledge base you maintain with an LLM,
151	  this is a knowledge base that maintains itself."*
152	- **[`tobi/qmd`](https://github.com/tobi/qmd)** — local search engine for
153	  markdown (hybrid BM25 + vector + LLM re-ranking, on-device). Has both a
154	  CLI for the LLM to shell out to and an MCP server. Mentioned by the
155	  gist as the natural upgrade path once the index file alone stops
156	  scaling.
157	- **Obsidian Web Clipper**, **Marp** (markdown-to-slides), **Dataview**
158	  (frontmatter queries) — the supporting tools the gist recommends.
159	
160	## Relation to this repo
161	
162	This repo's [`project-knowledge-harness`](../skills/project-knowledge-harness.md)
163	is **task memory** — `TODO.md` + `backlog/` + `pitfalls/`, oriented around
164	shipped/deferred work and past traps. Karpathy's LLM Wiki is **knowledge
165	memory** — a curated, synthesized view of an external research area. The
166	two are orthogonal and could coexist on the same project.
167	
168	Possible follow-ups (not committed):
169	
170	- Vendor `obsidian-second-brain` into `skills/vendor/` (license permitting),
171	  alongside `project-knowledge-harness` as a "two flavors of memory" pair.
172	- Author a minimal local `llm-wiki-bootstrap` skill — just the gist's
173	  three-layer architecture + `index.md` / `log.md` + `ingest` / `query` /
174	  `lint` commands, no Obsidian dependency.
175	
176	If you want to track either, add a `P3` entry via
177	[`scripts/add-todo.sh`](scripts.md).
178
```
</details></tool-use>

1	# Warp Oz skills
2	
3	[Warp](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp) (57k⭐) is a terminal that evolved into an
4	"agentic development environment." In May 2026 Warp open-sourced its main
5	codebase under **AGPL-3.0**. Alongside the main repo, the team publishes
6	[`warpdotdev/oz-skills`](https://github.com/warpdotdev/oz-skills) (764⭐)
7	— a growing collection of skills for their **Oz** cloud-agent platform.
8	
9	## Why oz-skills is installable here
10	
11	oz-skills is **MIT-licensed** and follows the
12	[agentskills.io specification](https://agentskills.io/specification), so
13	the skills work in any compliant agent: Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Cursor,
14	Gemini CLI. The Warp agent is just another host — the skills themselves are
15	portable markdown.
16	
17	The Warp main repo is AGPL-3.0 (viral copyleft); that license does **not**
18	propagate to oz-skills, which is separately MIT. Vendoring oz-skills into this
19	repo is safe.
20	
21	## Skills we vendor (6 of 15)
22	
23	We pick skills that fill genuine gaps in this repo's existing lineup. Skipped
24	skills: `mcp-builder` (duplicate of `anthropics/mcp-builder`), `webapp-testing`
25	(duplicate of `anthropics/webapp-testing` in the `fullstack-nextjs` series),
26	`scheduler` (too narrow — local-only reminders), `slack-qa-investigate` (Slack
27	dependency), `dbt-model-index` / `analysis-artifacts` (BigQuery-shaped for
28	Warp's internal stack), `terraform-style-check` (too narrow), `seo-aeo-audit`
29	(too opinionated), `docs-update` (overlaps `doc-coauthoring` / the doc-update
30	pattern already in CLAUDE.md).
31	
32	### `github-workflow` plugin — 4 skills
33	
34	| Skill | Description |
35	|---|---|
36	| `ci-fix` | Diagnose GitHub Actions failures: inspect logs via `gh`, identify root cause, implement a minimal fix, push to a dedicated fix branch. Prerequisite: `gh auth status`. |
37	| `create-pull-request` | Create a well-structured PR following project conventions — commit analysis, branch management, PR body via `gh pr create`. |
38	| `github-bug-report-triage` | Evaluate a GitHub bug issue for actionability. Locates the project's bug-report template, checks required fields, and drafts a constructive comment for incomplete reports. |
39	| `github-issue-dedupe` | Detect duplicate issues using multi-strategy semantic + keyword search. Can run manually or be wired into a GitHub Actions workflow. |
40	
41	These complement `engineering-fundamentals/triage` (mattpocock) which is more
42	general-purpose. The Oz skills are GitHub-specific and use the `gh` CLI for
43	automation.
44	
45	### `web-quality` plugin — 2 skills
46	
47	| Skill | Description |
48	|---|---|
49	| `web-accessibility-audit` | WCAG 2.0/2.1/2.2 compliance audit — identifies violations by POUR principle category, provides remediation steps. Works without an MCP dependency. |
50	| `web-performance-audit` | Core Web Vitals + Lighthouse audit using the `chrome-devtools` MCP. Requires `chrome-devtools-mcp@latest` configured in `.mcp.json`. If not configured, the skill tells you how to add it. |
51	
52	`web-accessibility-audit` is MCP-free and works anywhere. `web-performance-audit`
53	requires the Chrome DevTools MCP — the skill gracefully degrades if it is not
54	present.
55	
56	## Install
57	
58	```bash
59	# All 6 via this repo
60	npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills
61	
62	# Or directly from upstream
63	npx skills@latest add warpdotdev/oz-skills/.agents/skills/ci-fix
64	npx skills@latest add warpdotdev/oz-skills/.agents/skills/web-accessibility-audit
65	# ...
66	```
67	
68	## Warp's AGPL-3.0 note
69	
70	The Warp terminal itself is AGPL-3.0. If you embed Warp into a product you
71	ship to users, AGPL requires you to open-source your modifications. Using Warp
72	as a local development tool does not trigger AGPL. Using oz-skills (MIT)
73	separately from Warp has no AGPL implications.
74	
75	## See also
76	
77	- [Browser automation skills](browser-automation-skills.md) — testing web apps
78	  in a real browser; complements the web-quality skills above
79	- [`fullstack-nextjs/webapp-testing`](../skills/webapp-testing.md) — the
80	  Playwright-based Anthropic skill already vendored for frontend QA
81	- [Agent skill compatibility](agent-skill-compatibility.md) — portable

1	# Deep Research landscape
2	
3	This page surveys the **commercial Deep Research products** from major AI
4	vendors and the **open-source skills/frameworks** that try to reproduce
5	similar capability locally. It also explains what this repo vendors
6	(`deep-research/`) and which adjacent options are deliberately *not*
7	vendored.
8	
9	## Commercial Deep Research products (2024–2026)
10	
11	The five major vendors converged on a similar shape — multi-agent
12	planning, parallel retrieval, citation-grounded synthesis — but with
13	different defaults around browser scope, model size, and pricing.
14	
15	| Vendor | Product | Launched | Architecture | Notable |
16	|---|---|---|---|---|
17	| **OpenAI** | ChatGPT Deep Research (`o3-deep-research`, `o4-mini-deep-research`) | 2025-02 | Plan → multi-step search → cited report | Plus 25/mo, Pro 250/mo; 2026-02 added scoped sites + collaborative planning + live progress |
18	| **Google** | Gemini Deep Research (Interactions API) | 2024-12 | Lead agent + parallel sub-agents + synthesis agent | Hooks into Gmail/Drive/Chat; 1M-token context; Canvas visualizations; 2026-04 added MCP tool connectors |
19	| **xAI** | Grok DeepSearch / DeeperSearch / Grok 4 Heavy | 2024-Q2 → 2025-07 | Multi-agent parallel reasoning, live X + web search | 256k token context; no formal citations yet; emphasizes raw performance |
20	| **Anthropic** | Claude Research | 2025-06 (eng blog) | LeadResearcher + sub-agents + CitationAgent | ~90% accuracy uplift over single-agent (Opus 4 lead + Sonnet 4 sub); strict enterprise privacy |
21	| **Meta** | (no first-party DR product) | — | — | LLaMA 4 Scout/Maverick are multimodal foundation models; deep-research must be assembled from LangChain / LlamaIndex / vector DBs |
22	
23	The shared pattern across all four shipping products:
24	
25	1. **Plan** — decompose query into sub-questions
26	2. **Parallel retrieve** — spawn sub-agents that hit web search / docs / files
27	3. **Iterate** — re-plan based on what's found, follow citations
28	4. **Synthesize** — assemble a cited report (markdown / HTML / PDF)
29	
30	Typical wall time is 2–20 minutes; cost is gated by subscription tier or
31	per-call API metering.
32	
33	## Reproducing Deep Research locally — the six layers
34	
35	A real "deep research" stack for an agent CLI is **not a single skill**.
36	Decompose it into six layers; pick a tool per layer:
37	
38	| Layer | What it does | Representative tools |
39	|---|---|---|
40	| 1. **Planning / decomposition** | Turn the question into sub-questions, evidence requirements, and a research plan | `199-biotechnologies/claude-deep-research-skill` (vendored), `langchain-ai/deepagents` (Python framework, *not* a skill) |
41	| 2. **Retrieval** | Web / news / GitHub / PDF search | [`tavily-ai/skills/tavily-search`](https://github.com/tavily-ai/skills), [`firecrawl/cli/skills/firecrawl-search`](https://github.com/firecrawl/cli) |
42	| 3. **Extraction** | Pull main content, tables, multi-page text out of fetched URLs | `firecrawl-scrape`, `firecrawl-crawl`, `firecrawl-parse` |
43	| 4. **Browser interaction** | Login walls, JS rendering, dynamic UIs, downloads | [`vercel-labs/agent-browser`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-browser) (32k⭐), [`browser-use/browser-use`](https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use) (93k⭐) |
44	| 5. **Evidence management** | Source registry, claim ledger, citation verification | `199-biotechnologies/claude-deep-research-skill` (built-in) |
45	| 6. **Synthesis** | Final report (markdown / HTML / PDF) with inline citations | `199-biotechnologies/claude-deep-research-skill`, `tavily-ai/skills/tavily-research` |
46	
47	The 2-skill minimum that gets you something usable: **(1) + (5) + (6)**
48	from one disciplined research-flow skill, plus **(2)** from a search
49	backend you trust.
50	
51	## What this repo vendors
52	
53	Just **one** skill, deliberately:
54	
55	- **`vendor/deep-research/deep-research`** — from
56	  [`199-biotechnologies/claude-deep-research-skill`](https://github.com/199-biotechnologies/claude-deep-research-skill)
57	  (646⭐). A pure prompt-flow skill covering planning, evidence
58	  management, and synthesis. Four modes: `quick` (3 phases, 2–5 min),
59	  `standard` (6 phases, 5–10 min, default), `deep` (8 phases,
60	  10–20 min), `ultradeep` (8+ phases, 20–45 min). Uses an evidence
61	  ledger + claim ledger so each finding traces back to its source.
62	
63	**Why only one?** Deep-research stacks built from
64	[`tavily-ai/skills`](https://github.com/tavily-ai/skills),
65	[`firecrawl/cli`](https://github.com/firecrawl/cli),
66	[`vercel-labs/agent-browser`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-browser),
67	or [`browser-use/browser-use`](https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use)
68	all introduce **paid API keys, hosted backends, or cloud browser
69	sessions**. Keeping this repo cost-free by default means anyone can run
70	the vendored research skill against whatever search/browser tools their
71	agent already has (`WebSearch`, `WebFetch`, MCP, etc.) without signing
72	up for a third-party service.
73	
74	If you want a higher-fidelity pipeline, install those skills *alongside*
75	this one — they compose cleanly.
76	
77	## Adjacent options *not* vendored — and why
78	
79	Recorded so future agents don't relitigate it:
80	
81	| Option | Stars | Why not vendored |
82	|---|---:|---|
83	| [`tavily-ai/skills`](https://github.com/tavily-ai/skills) | 285⭐ | Requires Tavily account / API key. Excellent if you're willing to pay; install separately when you are. |
84	| [`firecrawl/cli`](https://github.com/firecrawl/cli) | 375⭐ | 9 skills (search/scrape/crawl/map/extract/agent…). Free tier exists but production use needs a key. Better as a per-project install. |
85	| [`vercel-labs/agent-browser`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-browser) | 32k⭐ | Browser automation is a heavy dependency (Chromium, profiles). Out of scope for a research-only stack; install if you actually need it. |
86	| [`browser-use/browser-use`](https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use) | 93k⭐ | Skills.sh shows a failed Gen Agent Trust Hub security audit. Skip until that resolves. |
87	| [`langchain-ai/deepagents`](https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents) | 22k⭐ | **Not a `SKILL.md` repo** — it's a Python package / framework. Cannot be vendored as an agent skill. ChatGPT-style summaries sometimes mislabel it. |
88	| [`24601/agent-deep-research`](https://github.com/24601/agent-deep-research) | 4⭐ | Genuine Gemini Interactions API wrapper, but too small / experimental to commit to. Worth re-evaluating later. |
89	
90	### Things that *look* like deep-research skills but aren't
91	
92	- [`forrestchang/andrej-karpathy-skills`](https://github.com/forrestchang/andrej-karpathy-skills)
93	  (124k⭐) — name and star count are misleading. It's **a single
94	  `CLAUDE.md`** distilling four Karpathy observations on LLM coding
95	  pitfalls. Not a skill, not about research. See
96	  [Karpathy's LLM Wiki pattern](llm-wiki-pattern.md) for the
97	  *separate* knowledge-base pattern Karpathy actually published in his
98	  [LLM Wiki gist](https://gist.github.com/karpathy/442a6bf555914893e9891c11519de94f).
99	
100	## See also
101	
102	- [Karpathy's LLM Wiki pattern](llm-wiki-pattern.md) — the persistent
103	  knowledge-base pattern that complements deep research (research
104	  produces reports; the wiki accumulates them)
105	- [SDD frameworks & agent harnesses](sdd-and-harnesses.md) — same
106	  layering distinction (skill / framework / harness) applied to
107	  spec-driven development
108	- [Skill risk evaluations](skills-risk-evaluations.md) — how to decide
109	  whether a workflow should become a skill at all
110
```

1	# Financial data sources skill set
2	
3	**Status**: P?
4	**Effort**: L
5	**Related**: `TODO.md` · `README.md` · `vendor.yaml`
6	
7	## Context
8	
9	This topic started as a nested subtree in the old `TODO.md` covering a mix of
10	free and paid data vendors across US, Taiwan, and China markets. It needs to be
11	handled as one evaluation item first, because the real question is not "which
12	provider should we write about next?" but "what shape should a reusable market
13	data skill take in this repo?"
14	
15	## Investigation
16	
17	The original idea list bundled these candidates together:
18	
19	- Yahoo Finance (`yfinance`)
20	- Alpha Vantage
21	- Quandl
22	- FRED
23	- IEX Cloud
24	- Polygon.io
25	- Tiingo
26	- TWSE
27	- AKShare
28	- Wind
29	- JoinQuant
30	- Tushare
31	
32	The list mixes several dimensions that should probably not be decided ad hoc:
33	
34	- Free vs paid APIs
35	- Retail-friendly vs institution-oriented products
36	- US-focused vs Taiwan/China-focused coverage
37	- Raw market-data access vs research workflows built on top of the data
38	
39	No code spike has been done yet. The next useful step is to decide the intended
40	user and coverage model before splitting this into implementation-sized skills.
41	
42	## Options considered
43	
44	| Option | Pros | Cons |
45	|---|---|---|
46	| One skill per provider | Precise and easy to scope | Duplicates setup and decision logic across providers |
47	| One workflow-oriented umbrella skill | Captures provider trade-offs in one place | Risks becoming too broad without strong boundaries |
48	| Tiered approach: umbrella guide plus provider deep-dives | Gives users a decision layer and implementation details | Higher maintenance cost and requires consistent cross-linking |
49	
50	## Current blocker / open questions
51	
52	- Which audience matters first: general Python quants, Taiwan/China market users, or broader agent-skill consumers?
53	- Should this repo optimize for accessible/free providers first, or is paid-data coverage acceptable?
54	- Do we want a single decision-oriented skill first, or direct provider-specific implementation guides?
55	
56	## Decision (if any)
57	
58	2026-04 deferred. Keep this as one research-backed `P?` item until the audience
59	and grouping strategy are explicit.
60	
61	## References
62	
63	- `TODO.md` historical source list under "Financial Data Sources"
64	- `README.md` "Available Skills" section for how this repo currently presents skill families
65

1	# Browser automation skills & MCPs
2	
3	This page compares the popular **browser automation tools shipped as
4	agent skills or MCP servers**. Browser automation is one of the highest-
5	value capabilities you can give a coding agent — but the design choices
6	across these tools differ substantially. This page records the trade-offs
7	so the choice is explicit, and explains why this repo currently does
8	*not* vendor any of them.
9	
10	## At a glance
11	
12	Five well-known options, all roughly the same goal — let an agent open a
13	real browser and interact with pages — but very different shapes:
14	
15	| Tool | ⭐ | Form | Auth/session | Cost model | Token-efficient surface |
16	|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
17	| [`microsoft/playwright-cli`](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright-cli) | 10k | CLI + 1 SKILL.md | Local Chromium / your profile | Free, local | a11y-tree snapshot + `eN` refs |
18	| [`vercel-labs/agent-browser`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-browser) | 33k | CLI + 1 SKILL.md | Local Chromium, profile, Vercel Sandbox, AWS Bedrock AgentCore cloud | Free CLI; Vercel/AWS pay-as-you-go for cloud | a11y-tree snapshot + compact `@eN` refs |
19	| [`browser-use/browser-use`](https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use) | 93k | CLI + 4 SKILL.md (`browser-use`, `cloud`, `open-source`, `remote-browser`) | Local + Browser Use Cloud | Open-source local; Cloud SaaS | Persistent daemon (~50 ms/call); MCP also available |
20	| [`browserbase/stagehand`](https://github.com/browserbase/stagehand) | 23k | TypeScript SDK | Browserbase cloud (or local Playwright) | Browserbase metered | Code-first (`page.act("click sign in")`); not a SKILL.md |
21	| [Playwright MCP](https://playwright.dev/agent-cli/introduction) | (part of Playwright) | MCP server | Local Chromium | Free, local | a11y tree, but full MCP schema overhead |
22	
23	> Star counts are repo totals (the project, not just the skill). Don't
24	> use them to compare per-skill quality — `browser-use/browser-use` is a
25	> framework with very high stars; the SKILL.md inside it is one
26	> deliverable among many.
27	
28	## The design axes that actually matter
29	
30	Pick on these, not on stars:
31	
32	### 1. CLI vs MCP vs SDK
33	
34	- **CLI + SKILL.md** — `playwright-cli`, `agent-browser`, `browser-use`
35	  (CLI mode). The agent shells out to `playwright-cli click e15`. Each
36	  command is one short tool call; no MCP schema to load. **Best for
37	  token efficiency** when the agent has Bash access. The Microsoft
38	  README and the agent-browser README both argue this beats the MCP
39	  approach for high-throughput agent loops.
40	- **MCP server** — Playwright MCP, `browser-use` MCP. The agent calls
41	  `mcp_call("playwright.click", {...})`. Loads the full schema once;
42	  cleaner for agents without Bash but pays the MCP overhead. Token cost
43	  per call is higher than CLI for the same operation.
44	- **SDK** — Stagehand. You write TypeScript that calls `page.act("…")`.
45	  Powerful for *application code* you ship; not a skill the agent
46	  invokes ad-hoc.
47	
48	### 2. Snapshot strategy — a11y tree vs DOM vs vision
49	
50	- **Accessibility-tree snapshot + element refs** (`playwright-cli`,
51	  `agent-browser`, Playwright MCP). The agent sees a structured tree
52	  with stable `eN` / `@eN` refs and uses them directly. Token-cheap,
53	  reliable, no fragile selectors.
54	- **DOM + selectors** (older Playwright / Selenium patterns). Larger
55	  context, brittle.
56	- **Vision-first** (`magnitudedev/browser-agent`, 4k⭐). Agent reasons
57	  over screenshots. Robust against DOM changes; high token + latency
58	  cost; useful when the page is an opaque webapp.
59	
60	### 3. Where the browser actually runs
61	
62	- **Local Chromium** (default for all CLIs above) — fast, free, uses
63	  your machine.
64	- **Local Chrome with your real profile** (`agent-browser`,
65	  `browser-use`) — sees your real cookies and logged-in state. Powerful;
66	  also a security surface.
67	- **Cloud browser** — Vercel Sandbox / AWS Bedrock AgentCore
68	  (`agent-browser`); Browser Use Cloud (`browser-use`); Browserbase
69	  (`stagehand`). Pay-per-session; required for headless servers, scale,
70	  or compliance.
71	
72	### 4. Persistent session vs cold-start per call
73	
74	- **Persistent daemon** (`browser-use` CLI) — keeps Chromium alive
75	  between commands; ~50 ms per call. Best for long agent loops on the
76	  same site.
77	- **Per-call session** (`playwright-cli` defaults, Playwright MCP) —
78	  starts/stops cleanly; safer for one-shot tasks. Higher per-call latency.
79	
80	## Recommendation matrix
81	
82	| Need | Pick |
83	|---|---|
84	| Token-efficient browser CLI for any agent with Bash | `agent-browser` or `playwright-cli` |
85	| Already on Playwright in CI | `playwright-cli` (same engine, same selectors) |
86	| Long-running session, lowest per-call latency | `browser-use` CLI |
87	| Production agents, cloud parallel browsers | `agent-browser` (Vercel/AWS) or `stagehand` (Browserbase) |
88	| Pages that defeat DOM scraping (heavy canvases, anti-bot) | Vision-first (`magnitudedev/browser-agent`) |
89	| Want code-level control inside a TypeScript app | `stagehand` SDK |
90	| Agent doesn't have Bash, only MCP | Playwright MCP or `browser-use` MCP |
91	
92	## What this repo vendors
93	
94	**None of these.** Recorded so future agents don't relitigate it:
95	
96	- **Heavy install surface** — Chromium download, persistent profiles,
97	  daemon processes, optional cloud accounts. Vendoring as a SKILL.md
98	  doesn't actually install the underlying CLI; users still need
99	  `npm i -g agent-browser`, `pip install browser-use`, etc.
100	- **Per-project rather than user-global** — browser automation skills
101	  often touch real auth/cookies and per-site quirks. Better installed
102	  per project where the operator can review the SKILL.md, hooks, and
103	  any MCP config first.
104	- **Security audit signal** — Skills.sh shows a failed Gen Agent Trust
105	  Hub audit on `browser-use/browser-use` at the time of writing. Good
106	  enough reason to defer until the situation clarifies.
107	- **Anthropic `webapp-testing` already covers the common case** — for
108	  agent-driven QA of a web app this repo already vendors
109	  [`anthropics/skills/webapp-testing`](../skills/webapp-testing.md)
110	  under the [`fullstack-nextjs`](../skills/index.md) series, which uses
111	  Playwright under the hood without committing to a specific browser
112	  CLI.
113	
114	If you decide you need one, install per project:
115	
116	```bash
117	# Token-efficient CLI route (recommended for OpenCode / Claude Code / Codex)
118	npx skills add vercel-labs/agent-browser
119	
120	# Long-running daemon route
121	npx skills add browser-use/browser-use
122	
123	# Same engine as your CI Playwright tests
124	npx skills add microsoft/playwright-cli
125	```
126	
127	These compose with this repo's research and SDD skills — a deep-research
128	session that needs a real browser can pair `vendor/deep-research` with
129	any of the above without conflict.
130	
131	## See also
132	
133	- [Deep Research landscape](deep-research-landscape.md) — browser
134	  automation is layer 4 in the deep-research stack
135	- [SDD frameworks & agent harnesses](sdd-and-harnesses.md) — same
136	  CLI vs MCP vs framework distinction applied to spec-driven dev
137	- [`anthropics/webapp-testing`](../skills/webapp-testing.md) — the
138	  Playwright-based testing skill already vendored in this repo
139	- [Agent skill compatibility](agent-skill-compatibility.md) — portable
140	  `SKILL.md` constraints all the CLIs above respect
141
```

```text
1	# Spec-Driven Development frameworks & agent harnesses
2	
3	This page surveys the popular **spec-driven development (SDD)** frameworks
4	and **agent harnesses** that sit *one layer above* agent skills, and records
5	where this repo intentionally does not compete with them.
6	
7	## The layering
8	
9	Three things often get conflated. They are not the same:
10	
11	| Layer | What it is | Examples |
12	|---|---|---|
13	| **Skill** | A small `SKILL.md` (+ optional `references/`, `scripts/`) the agent loads on demand. Stateless prompt fragment. Governed by the [Agent Skills spec](https://agentskills.io/specification). | This repo's skills, `mattpocock/skills`, `anthropics/skills`, `gstack` skills |
14	| **SDD framework** | A workflow that owns the loop *requirements → spec → plan → tasks → execute → verify*, usually via slash commands and structured artifacts. Stateful (writes spec/plan/task files into the repo). | [`github/spec-kit`](https://github.com/github/spec-kit), [`gsd-build/get-shit-done`](https://github.com/gsd-build/get-shit-done) |
15	| **Agent harness** | A standalone CLI/runtime that *controls* the agent session — context windows, fresh subagents, git worktrees, crash recovery, cost tracking. Replaces or wraps the agent. | [`gsd-build/gsd-2`](https://github.com/gsd-build/gsd-2), [OpenClaw](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw), [Pi SDK](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono) |
16	
17	Skills are *consumed* by harnesses and SDD frameworks. They are not a
18	substitute for either. This repo focuses on **skills**, and explicitly does
19	not ship a SDD framework or harness.
20	
21	## Surveyed projects
22	
23	### `github/spec-kit` (95.5k ⭐) — the SDD reference implementation
24	
25	The de facto SDD framework, maintained by GitHub. Installs a Python CLI
26	(`specify`) plus a set of slash commands that write spec/plan/task artifacts
27	into your repo:
28	
29	| Command | What it produces |
30	|---|---|
31	| `/speckit.constitution` | `.specify/memory/` — project governing principles |
32	| `/speckit.specify` | Feature spec (the *what* and *why*, not the stack) |
33	| `/speckit.plan` | Technical implementation plan (the *how*) |
34	| `/speckit.tasks` | Actionable task list |
35	| `/speckit.implement` | Execute tasks |
36	| `/speckit.clarify`, `/speckit.analyze`, `/speckit.checklist` | Optional quality gates |
37	
38	Key properties:
39	
40	- **Open ecosystem** — 80+ community extensions in [the catalog](https://github.com/github/spec-kit/blob/main/extensions/catalog.community.json)
41	  (Jira/Linear sync, security review, V-Model, brownfield bootstrap, retro,
42	  etc.) plus presets that override templates without touching tooling.
43	- **30+ supported agents** — Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, Windsurf,
44	  Gemini CLI, Kilo, etc.
45	- **Skills mode** — `--integration <agent> --integration-options="--skills"`
46	  installs the slash commands as agent skills (`speckit-constitution`,
47	  `speckit-plan`, …) instead of slash-command files.
48	- **Stateless** — spec-kit itself doesn't manage agent sessions; it just
49	  writes prompt files and lets your agent execute.
50	
51	### `gsd-build/get-shit-done` (61.4k ⭐) — opinionated SDD for solo builders
52	
53	Earlier, lighter take on the same idea, by TÂCHES. Six-command loop:
54	
55	```
56	/gsd-new-project → /gsd-discuss-phase → /gsd-plan-phase
57	  → /gsd-execute-phase → /gsd-verify-work → /gsd-ship
58	```
59	
60	Differentiators vs spec-kit:
61	
62	- **Fewer ceremonies** — explicitly built for solo devs, not 50-person eng
63	  orgs. No story points, no sprint syncs.
64	- **Subagent orchestration baked in** — execute runs plans in *parallel
65	  waves*, each in its own fresh 200k-token context.
66	- **Persistent artifacts** — `PROJECT.md` / `REQUIREMENTS.md` /
67	  `ROADMAP.md` / `STATE.md` / `CONTEXT.md` survive session boundaries so
68	  every fresh agent loads the same memory.
69	- Still a **prompt framework** — relies on the LLM following the prompts,
70	  no direct control over context or session lifecycle.
71	
72	### `gsd-build/gsd-2` (7.3k ⭐) — GSD as a real harness
73	
74	The successor that admits the prompt-framework approach has hard limits
75	(no context control, no crash recovery, no real automation) and rebuilds
76	GSD as a **standalone TypeScript CLI** on top of the [Pi SDK](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono).
77	Now an actual *agent harness*:
78	
79	| v1 (prompt framework) | v2 (agent harness) |
80	|---|---|
```

1	# quantatitive-factor-researcher
2	
3	A persona-style skill that turns the agent into a quantitative factor
4	researcher for Python-based investment-strategy work. Use it when the user
5	wants help designing, evaluating, or implementing factor-based strategies
6	end-to-end: data acquisition → feature engineering → signal testing →
7	risk control → backtest and performance evaluation.
8	
9	## When the skill triggers
10	
11	- The user asks for help building or analysing alpha / risk factors.
12	- The user mentions tools like `pandas`, `numpy`, `scikit-learn`,
13	  `vectorbt`, `PyTorch`, MLflow, or DVC in the context of trading research.
14	- The user wants performance metrics interpreted (Sharpe Ratio, IR,
15	  Tracking Error, Drawdown, etc.).
16	- The user requests time-series-aware cross-validation (Purged
17	  Group-Time-Series Split, walk-forward).
18	
19	Do **not** use this skill for general Python coding, generic data
20	analysis, or unrelated finance topics (accounting, macro forecasts) —
21	those don't benefit from the persona overhead.
22	
23	## Structure of the skill
24	
25	```
26	skills/local/quantatitive-factor-researcher/
27	└── SKILL.md   # persona + responsibilities + style/technical conventions
28	```
29	
30	Single-file skill — no `assets/`, `scripts/`, or `references/`. The
31	content is mostly persona + style guidance, which is the "right size" for
32	inline content. If future additions grow beyond ~500 lines (e.g.,
33	reusable backtest scaffolding, evaluation report templates), promote the
34	extra material into `references/` and `assets/` rather than letting
35	`SKILL.md` swell.
36	
37	## What the skill encodes
38	
39	### Core responsibilities
40	
41	1. Provide a rigorous, reproducible quant-research pipeline.
42	2. Write and explain high-quality Python with type hints and English
43	   comments.
44	3. Explore and optimise alpha / risk factors with statistical and ML
45	   methods (genetic algorithms, tree models, deep learning, Bayesian).
46	4. When useful, supply LaTeX (English variables) and Matplotlib / Plotly
47	   chart suggestions to explain methodology and results.
48	5. Interpret backtest metrics and suggest improvements.
49	
50	### Language & style rules
51	
52	- If the user opens in Chinese, reply in Traditional Chinese with
53	  English terminology in parentheses; specialist terms always carry the
54	  English form.
55	- LaTeX formulas use English variables and comments.
56	- Python comments are in English; every function has type annotations
57	  and a docstring.
58	- Replies are structured (sections, bullets) but not verbose.
59	- External references (papers, GitHub repos, datasets) include full
60	  citation format.
61	
62	### Technical conventions
63	
64	- Vectorised operations and built-ins by default; explain parallel /
65	  GPU acceleration when relevant.
66	- Configuration-driven pipelines, with hooks into MLflow / DVC for
67	  experiment tracking.
68	- Strict against data leakage: Purged Group-Time-Series Split,
69	  walk-forward validation, out-of-sample testing.
70	
71	## Limitations and known gaps
72	
73	- The skill ships no example notebooks or backtest scaffolding yet — it
74	  is purely a persona. Adding `assets/` with reusable factor-evaluation
75	  scaffolds is a candidate `[?/L]` item for [`TODO.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/blob/main/TODO.md).
76	- It does not currently bundle a "preferred data source" decision —
77	  that interacts with the broader "Financial data sources skill set"
78	  P? item already in the repo backlog.
79
```

1	# CLAUDE.md
2	
3	This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
4	
5	## Project Overview
6	
7	A personal agent skills collection installable via `npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills`. Contains custom-authored skills (`skills/local/`) and cherry-picked 3rd-party skills (`skills/vendor/`) synced from upstream repos.
8	
9	The skills CLI discovers skills by checking `skills/` one level deep for `SKILL.md`, then falls back to recursive search (up to 5 levels). The nested `local/`/`vendor/` structure works because of this fallback behavior — including vendor `series` subdirs (e.g. `skills/vendor/fullstack-nextjs/<name>/SKILL.md` at depth 4).
10	
11	## Commands
12	
13	```bash
14	# Sync all vendored skills from upstream
15	make sync
16	
17	# Check for upstream updates (dry-run)
18	make sync-check
19	
20	# Validate and render the repo backlog board
21	make kanban
22	
23	# Validate skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json (the catalog manifest
24	# that drives the grouped install UI of `npx skills add ...`).
25	make marketplace
26	
27	# Add a new vendored skill (auto-syncs)
28	./scripts/add-vendor.sh owner/repo/path/to/skill
29	./scripts/add-vendor.sh https://github.com/owner/repo/tree/branch/path/to/skill
30	# Group under a series subdir (skills/vendor/<series>/<name>/)
31	./scripts/add-vendor.sh --series fullstack-nextjs vercel/vercel-plugin/skills/nextjs
32	
33	# Add a structured TODO entry (preferred over editing TODO.md by hand)
34	./scripts/add-todo.sh --priority P3 --effort M \
35	  --title "Title" --description "Description"
36	
37	# Triage backlog/inbox.md (loose captures) into TODO.md
38	./scripts/sweep-inbox.sh             # interactive
39	./scripts/sweep-inbox.sh --batch     # only formalize parseable key=value lines
40	
41	# Move an active TODO item to ## Done with the right syntax
42	./scripts/promote-todo.sh --title "<substring>" --summary "<shipped summary>"
43	
44	# Create a new local skill
45	cd skills/local && npx skills@latest init [skill-name]
46	
47	# Docs site (MkDocs Material + llmstxt + copy-to-llm)
48	uv sync --extra docs
49	make docs-serve     # http://127.0.0.1:8000/
50	make docs-build     # produces ./site/
51	```
52	
53	## Vendor System
54	
55	- `vendor.yaml` — manifest of upstream skill sources with `last_sync` tracking (date + commit SHA). Optional per-entry `series:` field groups skills under `skills/vendor/<series>/<name>/`; entries without `series` stay flat at `skills/vendor/<name>/`
56	- `scripts/sync-vendor.sh` — downloads skill files via GitHub API (`gh` + `yq` required); honors the `series` field for nested destinations
57	- `scripts/add-vendor.sh` — adds entries to `vendor.yaml`, verifies upstream exists, deduplicates; pass `--series <name>` to group into a series subdir
58	
59	Sync uses the git trees API to recursively download skill directories (SKILL.md + references/ etc.) and updates `vendor.yaml` with the latest commit SHA.
60	
61	Active series in this repo:
62	- `fullstack-nextjs` — Next.js + Supabase + shadcn/ui + Tailwind + design/testing skills (9 skills from vercel/vercel-plugin, vercel-labs/agent-skills, supabase/agent-skills, anthropics/skills)
63	
64	## Marketplace Catalog
65	
66	`skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` defines the user-facing plugin
67	groupings shown by `npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills`.
68	Located under `skills/` (not repo root) because the `/skills` subpath in
69	the install command makes the CLI read the manifest from
70	`<repo>/skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` — see
71	[`docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md`](docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md)
72	for the full mechanism.
73	
74	When adding a new skill (local or vendored), also append its path to the
75	matching plugin's `skills[]` array in the manifest, or accept that it
76	will fall through to the **Other** group. Run `make marketplace` after
77	editing — the validator catches broken paths, duplicates, and reserved
78	marketplace names. Path format is `./local/<name>` or
79	`./vendor/<name>` (relative to `skills/`, not repo root).
80	
81	## SKILL.md Format
82	
83	Each skill is a directory containing a `SKILL.md` with YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) and markdown body with instructions, conventions, and examples. Vendored skills may include `references/` subdirectories.
84	
85	## Project Memory Workflow
86	
87	### Long-term backlog -> `TODO.md` + `backlog/`
88	
89	When work is explicitly deferred, add it to [`TODO.md`](TODO.md) using the
90	fixed section order `P1`, `P2`, `P3`, `P?`, `Done`.
91	
92	- Active items must use `- [ ] **[Effort] Title** — description`
93	- `P?` items must use `- [ ] **[?/Effort] Title** — description`
94	- Non-trivial research should be linked as `→ [research](backlog/<slug>.md)`
95	
96	`TODO.md` is parsed by [`scripts/todo-kanban.sh`](scripts/todo-kanban.sh), so
97	do not invent alternate headings, nested bullets, or ad hoc checkbox formats.
98	
99	#### Three ways to add a TODO entry (preferred order)
100	
101	1. **Structured CLI — `scripts/add-todo.sh`** (default):
102	
103	   ```bash
104	   ./scripts/add-todo.sh --priority P3 --effort M \
105	     --title "Title" --description "Description"
106	   # add --backlog to also scaffold backlog/<slug>.md
107	   ```
108	
109	   This inserts a canonically-formatted line into the right `## P*` lane
110	   and re-runs the validator. Refuses to write a malformed entry.
111	
112	2. **Quick capture — `backlog/inbox.md`** (when priority/effort unclear):
113	
114	   ```bash
115	   echo "- maybe add docs versioning with mike" >> backlog/inbox.md
116	   ```
117	
118	   When the user asks "sweep the inbox" or "clear inbox.md", run
119	   [`./scripts/sweep-inbox.sh`](scripts/sweep-inbox.sh). It prompts for
120	   priority/effort/title/description per loose line and calls
121	   `add-todo.sh`. Use `--batch` for non-interactive runs that only
122	   formalize lines with parseable `key=value` pairs.
123	
124	3. **Direct edit of `TODO.md`** — fine if the format is fresh in your
125	   head; run `make kanban` (or `./scripts/todo-kanban.sh --validate-only`)
126	   afterwards to catch drift.
127	
128	#### Promote a TODO when implementing it
129	
130	When implementing a TODO item, in the same commit run:
131	
132	```bash
133	./scripts/promote-todo.sh --title "<substring>" --summary "<one-line shipped summary>"
134	```
135	
136	That moves the matched active item into `## Done` with the dated `Done`
137	syntax and re-validates the file. If a `backlog/<slug>.md` exists for the
138	item, also mark it as shipped (don't delete — keep it as historical record).
139	
140	Keep `## Done` as the recent history buffer. Prune it into `CHANGELOG.md` only
141	when it contains items from a previous calendar year or grows past 20 entries.
142

152	
153	Use symptom-first titles so future agents can grep the failure they see, not
154	the explanation they do not know yet.

# Docs-structure refactor — domains, external catalog, MCP wiki

Status: planning (read-only mode)
Date: 2026-05-13
Related: Collections.md migration, README "Resources" expansion, TODO.md P? items (financial-data-sources, VectorBT, Tardis, MLflow, DVC, fine-tuning, Gradio), https://docs.financialdatasets.ai/mcp-server

## TL;DR — recommended choices

1. **Domains**: ship as a new top-level `Catalog` parent that contains a `domains/` index + per-domain hub pages (option A). Do **not** reorganize `docs/skills/` (option B). Optionally surface a "by-domain" axis inside `docs/skills/index.md` (a slim version of option C) once at least two domain hubs exist.
2. **External skills**: migrate `Collections.md` into `docs/catalog/skill-collections.md` as a single curated index page; only spin off per-collection subpages (like `warp-oz-skills.md` already does) when a collection earns a dedicated page (>3 vendored skills, or significant install/license nuance worth its own page).
3. **MCP wiki**: new `docs/catalog/mcp/` section with `index.md` + per-MCP pages. Use a YAML frontmatter schema so the index can be a generated table later. First entry: `financialdatasets-ai.md`.
4. **Manual install pattern**: a small reusable include (`docs/_snippets/external-install.md`) plus a per-entry frontmatter block. Always include both `npx skills add ...` and the upstream URL; only call out vendoring decisions when the answer is "no, intentionally" with a stated reason.
5. **Nav reshuffle**: introduce a single new top-level **Catalog** parent (Domains, External skills, MCP wiki), and leave Skills / Workflows / Reference / Conventions where they are. This adds **one** sidebar item, not three. `Reference` stays for *meta* docs (formats, recipes, compatibility); `Catalog` is for *external awareness*.
6. **First PR**: ship Collections migration + the new `Catalog` nav skeleton + one finance domain hub + the financialdatasets-ai MCP page. Skip the rest.
7. **Bilingual cost**: every new page needs a `.zh-TW.md` sibling. Three new pages in PR1 (`catalog/index`, `catalog/skill-collections`, `catalog/domains/finance`, `catalog/mcp/index`, `catalog/mcp/financialdatasets-ai`) = 5 EN + 5 zh-TW = **10 files**. Honest cost: ~1 working session per language for translation if doing it carefully; the `mkdocs-i18n` `fallback_to_default: true` means a missing zh-TW page falls back to English so we can land EN-only and translate in a follow-up commit if needed.

---

## Q1. Where do domain hubs live?

**Recommend (A) with a twist: nest under a new top-level `Catalog` parent.**

| Option | Verdict | Why |
|---|---|---|
| (A) New `docs/domains/` section | **Pick** (under `docs/catalog/domains/` to share a parent with external skills + MCP wiki) | Minimal disruption. Hubs read like the existing `reference/*-landscape.md` pages but indexed as their own thing. Lets us add a domain by writing one file. |
| (B) Reorganize `docs/skills/` by domain | Reject | Current flat list works because `vendor.yaml` `series:` already does the grouping; adding a `domain:` axis would require schema changes, marketplace.json reshuffle, and rewriting `skills/index.md` tables. Out of scope. |
| (C) "By-domain" view inside `docs/skills/index.md` | Defer (use only as a small section once 2+ domain hubs exist) | Useful as a discovery aid but redundant with the hub pages. Add a "By domain" subsection that just links to `catalog/domains/*` once those exist. |

Each domain hub is a single page that links to:
- Local skills relevant to the domain (existing pages under `docs/skills/`)
- Vendored skills relevant to the domain (existing pages under `docs/skills/`)
- External skills (entries in `docs/catalog/skill-collections.md`)
- MCPs (pages under `docs/catalog/mcp/`)
- Backlog entries (`backlog/*.md` and TODO `P?` items)

Hubs are **awareness pages**, not registries. They explicitly do not duplicate the skill pages — they link to them. This is the same pattern as `reference/deep-research-landscape.md` ("what this repo vendors" + "adjacent options not vendored").

---

## Q2. Where does the external skills catalog live?

**Recommend: single curated index at `docs/catalog/skill-collections.md`. Spin off per-collection subpages only when warranted.**

Justification:
- `Collections.md` at repo root has 2 entries; the README "Resources" section has the curated 8 we actually care about. Reconciling these into one page kills the duplication.
- The existing `reference/warp-oz-skills.md` is the proof-of-concept for "one collection deserves its own page" (vendoring 6 of 15 skills, AGPL/MIT licensing nuance). That kind of depth justifies a subpage; the 2-line entries in the README "Resources" do not.
- The `reference/` section is for *meta* documentation (formats, recipes, compatibility specs, our own conventions). External upstream catalogs are **not** repo conventions — they're the world outside this repo. Conceptually different. New `Catalog` parent makes that distinction cleaner.
- Keep `warp-oz-skills.md` and `browser-automation-skills.md` and `deep-research-landscape.md` and `sdd-and-harnesses.md` where they are (`reference/`). They're hybrid — partly landscape, partly "why we vendor / why we don't". Migrating them would churn permalinks for no reader benefit. **Add cross-links from the new index, don't move existing pages.**

`Collections.md` at repo root: keep as a thin redirect comment ("→ docs/catalog/skill-collections.md") or delete. Recommend keep + redirect note, since some external readers may have linked it.

---

## Q3. Where does the MCP wiki live?

**Recommend: `docs/catalog/mcp/` with `index.md` + per-MCP pages.**

Per-category pages (`finance.md`, `dev-tools.md`) would force premature taxonomy decisions when we have one entry. Per-MCP pages let the index be a flat table that we can re-group later (or generate the table from frontmatter via a small script — see Q5 below).

**Per-MCP page schema** (YAML frontmatter + body):

\```yaml
---
name: Financial Datasets MCP
slug: financialdatasets-ai
upstream_url: https://docs.financialdatasets.ai/mcp-server
upstream_repo: https://github.com/financial-datasets/mcp-server  # optional
transport: [stdio, http, sse]   # which transports it offers
auth: [api_key, oauth]          # auth options
hosting: hosted                 # hosted | local | both
domain: [finance]               # cross-references docs/catalog/domains/*.md
status: documented              # documented | installed | considering
license: MIT                    # spdx
last_verified: "2026-05-13"
---
\```

**Body sections** (per page):
1. `## TL;DR` — one paragraph: what tools it exposes, why it exists, who runs it.
2. `## Tools / capabilities` — bullet list of MCP tools (e.g., `get_prices`, `get_company_facts`).
3. `## Auth & install` — copy-paste `.mcp.json` or `claude mcp add` snippet; note OAuth vs API-key paths.
4. `## When to use it` — bullets of trigger scenarios.
5. `## When NOT to use it` — explicit skip cases (cost, coverage gaps, geographic limits).
6. `## Related skills in this repo` — links to skills/domain hubs that pair with this MCP.
7. `## Upstream sources` — links to docs, repo, blog posts.

Index page (`docs/catalog/mcp/index.md`):
- Markdown table generated by hand initially (5 columns: Name, Domain, Auth, Transport, Page).
- Once the count exceeds ~6 entries, replace the manual table with a small script (see Q5) that reads frontmatter and emits the table at build time, so the index never goes stale.
- Add a "Why we don't auto-install MCPs" note explaining the personal-wiki-not-installer framing. This matches the `reference/llm-wiki-pattern.md` framing ("documentation, not a skill").

---

## Q4. Manual-install instructions — recommended template

Two reusable include snippets, plus a per-entry block at the top of each external entry:

### Snippet A — `docs/_snippets/external-install.md`

\```markdown
**Install** (manual, not vendored in this repo):

\```bash
# Single skill
npx skills@latest add OWNER/REPO/path/to/skill

# Whole collection
npx skills@latest add OWNER/REPO
\```

See [Adding vendor skills](../workflows/adding-vendor-skills.md) for how
this repo vendors skills upstream into `skills/vendor/<series>/<name>/`.
\```

(The actual snippet would be a real includable, with placeholders the entry overrides.)

### Per-entry block in `docs/catalog/skill-collections.md`

For each collection, a fenced section like:

\```markdown
### `RKiding/Awesome-finance-skills`

- **Upstream**: https://github.com/RKiding/Awesome-finance-skills
- **Vendored here?** No — curated awareness. (See [why](#vendoring-policy) below.)
- **Recommended skills to install**:
  - `npx skills add RKiding/Awesome-finance-skills/skills/<name>` — short blurb
- **Domain hub**: [Finance](domains/finance.md)
- **Last surveyed**: 2026-05-13
\```

### Vendoring decision footer (page-level, one section, not per-entry)

A single `## Vendoring policy` section at the bottom of `skill-collections.md`:

> Why most entries on this page are *not* vendored:
>
> - We vendor a skill only when (a) it covers a gap our own skills don't, (b) we'll keep the upstream sync running, and (c) including it in `marketplace.json` improves the install UX. Otherwise, **document and let users install per-project**. This keeps `vendor.yaml` from sprawling and keeps the repo install lean.

This avoids per-entry "why not vendored" bloat. Skills that earn vendoring move from this page into `docs/skills/index.md` and `vendor.yaml`, *with* a note here saying "vendored — see skills page".

## Q5. Navigation impact — proposed mkdocs.yml nav

**Add one parent (`Catalog`), keep the rest of the nav stable.**

\```yaml
nav:
  - Home: index.md
  - Getting Started: getting-started.md
  - Conventions: conventions.md
  - Workflows:
      - Adding vendor skills: workflows/adding-vendor-skills.md
      - Creating local skills: workflows/creating-local-skills.md
      - Project memory: workflows/project-memory.md
  - Skills:
      - Overview: skills/index.md
      - Local: ...                    # unchanged
      - Vendored: ...                 # unchanged
  - Catalog:
      - Overview: catalog/index.md
      - Domains:
          - Overview: catalog/domains/index.md
          - Finance: catalog/domains/finance.md
          # Future: catalog/domains/research.md, catalog/domains/web-dev.md, catalog/domains/ml-ops.md
      - External skills: catalog/skill-collections.md
      - MCP wiki:
          - Overview: catalog/mcp/index.md
          - Financial Datasets: catalog/mcp/financialdatasets-ai.md
          # Future per-MCP pages here
  - Reference:
      # unchanged — the existing 15 reference pages stay put.
      - TODO format: reference/todo-format.md
      - ...
  - Changelog: changelog.md
\```

Rationale:
- One new top-level item, three nested groups under it. With `navigation.sections` + `navigation.expand` already enabled, the sidebar is one click deeper but not bloated.
- `catalog/index.md` is a 1-screen landing page that explains what the three sub-sections are for and links to each.
- `Reference` is preserved for *meta* docs (formats, recipes, compatibility, our own landscape pages). Catalog is for *external awareness*.
- Existing landscape pages (`browser-automation-skills.md`, `deep-research-landscape.md`, `sdd-and-harnesses.md`, `warp-oz-skills.md`, `llm-wiki-pattern.md`) **do not move**. The new `catalog/index.md` cross-links to them with a "see also: landscape pages in Reference" callout.
- Add to `mkdocs.yml` `plugins.llmstxt.sections`:
  \```yaml
  Catalog:
    - catalog/*.md
    - catalog/domains/*.md
    - catalog/mcp/*.md
  \```
  so LLM consumers get the new section in `llms.txt` / `llms-full.txt`.

## Q7. Bilingual cost — honest accounting

For PR1, **5 new EN pages × 1 zh-TW each = 10 doc files**. The actual translation cost depends on how mechanical the page is:

- `catalog/index.md` — short, mostly a router. 30 min translation.
- `catalog/domains/index.md` — short. 30 min.
- `catalog/domains/finance.md` — medium-long (links + tables). 60–90 min.
- `catalog/skill-collections.md` — long (8+ entries with prose). 90–120 min.
- `catalog/mcp/index.md` — short. 30 min.
- `catalog/mcp/financialdatasets-ai.md` — medium. 60 min.

Total zh-TW translation: ~5 hours for PR1.

**Mitigation** (from `mkdocs.yml` already): `fallback_to_default: true` means a missing zh-TW page silently falls back to English. We can land PR1 EN-only and add zh-TW in a follow-up commit before declaring "shipped". This matches the precedent of `mkdocs-2-and-zensical.md` where the zh-TW version is intentionally short (689 bytes vs 1.5k EN) — an acceptable degradation.

(One block per collection — `vercel-labs/agent-skills`, `mattpocock/skills`,
`anthropics/skills`, `anthropics/knowledge-work-plugins`, `marimo-team/skills`,
`streamlit/agent-skills`. Each block uses the per-entry block template from
the plan's Q4.)

## Vendoring policy

Why most entries above are *not* vendored:

We vendor a skill into `skills/vendor/<series>/<name>/` only when:

1. It covers a gap our own skills don't already address.
2. We're committed to running `make sync` on it as upstream evolves.
3. Including it in `skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` improves the
   `npx skills add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills` install UX.

Otherwise, **document here and let users install per-project**. This
keeps `vendor.yaml` from sprawling and keeps the repo install lean. If a
collection earns its own page (significant licensing nuance, multi-skill
selection rationale, install caveats), it gets one — see
[`Warp Oz skills`](../reference/warp-oz-skills.md) and [`Browser automation
skills`](../reference/browser-automation-skills.md) for examples.
\```

# MCP wiki

Personal reference of [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io)
servers. **Documentation, not an installer** — entries here are recorded
because they're useful to know about, not because we ship them.

For our own MCP-authoring workflow, see the vendored
[`mcp-builder`](../../skills/skill-creator.md#related-skills) skill (from
`anthropics/skills`).

## Entries

| Server | Domain | Auth | Transport | Page |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Financial Datasets | Finance | API key, OAuth | stdio, http, sse | [page](financialdatasets-ai.md) |

## Why a wiki, not a registry?

Karpathy's [LLM Wiki pattern](../../reference/llm-wiki-pattern.md) — a
synthesized, curated knowledge base maintained by an LLM. MCP entries
here are knowledge memory: enough metadata to install if/when needed,
plus the trade-offs and "when *not* to use" notes that an MCP registry
won't tell you. They get updated when we re-evaluate, not on a schedule.

## Per-entry conventions

Every entry uses YAML frontmatter:

\```yaml
---
name: <Display name>
slug: <kebab-case>
upstream_url: <docs URL>
upstream_repo: <github URL>  # optional
transport: [stdio, http, sse]
auth: [api_key, oauth, none]
hosting: hosted | local | both
domain: [<domain slug>]
status: documented | installed | considering
license: <SPDX>
last_verified: "<YYYY-MM-DD>"
---
\```

See the [author template](#author-template) below for the body skeleton.
\```

# Financial Datasets MCP

A Model Context Protocol server providing financial market data —
prices, fundamentals, SEC filings — via API key or OAuth. Used by
[`anthropics/financial-services`](https://github.com/anthropics/financial-services).

## TL;DR

Call market data, financial statements, and SEC filings as MCP tools.
Hosted by financialdatasets.ai. Free tier covers basic equities; paid
tiers add coverage and rate.

## Tools / capabilities

(Confirm against upstream docs at next sync.)

- `get_prices(ticker, start, end, interval)` — historical OHLCV
- `get_company_facts(ticker)` — fundamentals, statements
- `get_filings(ticker, form_type, start, end)` — SEC filings
- ... (TODO: enumerate from upstream when verifying)

## Auth & install

Two auth paths:

- **API key** — set `FINANCIAL_DATASETS_API_KEY`, configure stdio transport.
- **OAuth** — for hosted Claude / multi-user use cases.

`.mcp.json` snippet (stdio + API key):

\```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "financialdatasets": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@financialdatasets/mcp-server"],
      "env": { "FINANCIAL_DATASETS_API_KEY": "${FINANCIAL_DATASETS_API_KEY}" }
    }
  }
}
\```

(Verify command name against upstream docs before relying on it.)

## When to use it

- You need US equities OHLCV / fundamentals inside a Claude Code session
  without writing your own data-loader.
- You're using `anthropics/financial-services` skills and want their data
  layer to "just work".
- You want OAuth-gated data access for a hosted agent (multi-user).

## When NOT to use it

- Non-US markets — coverage is US-equities-first; check upstream for
  international coverage before assuming.
- Crypto / forex / futures — out of scope.
- Tick / order-book data — Tardis SDK or a dedicated provider (see
  [Finance hub](../domains/finance.md) backlog).
- Anything where you want raw control over the rate/cost surface
  (running `yfinance` locally is free and immediate).

## Related skills in this repo

- [`quantatitive-factor-researcher`](../../skills/quantatitive-factor-researcher.md)
  — pairs with this MCP as the "data layer" of a factor pipeline.
- See [Finance hub](../domains/finance.md) for the rest.

## Upstream sources

- Docs: https://docs.financialdatasets.ai/mcp-server
- Used by: https://github.com/anthropics/financial-services
\```

# Docs-structure refactor plan — recommendations

## Headline choices

1. **Domain hubs**: option A, but nested under a new top-level **`Catalog`** parent. Path: `docs/catalog/domains/<domain>.md`. Reject option B (reorganizing `docs/skills/`) — `vendor.yaml` `series:` already does the grouping that matters; flipping to a domain axis would force `marketplace.json` and `vendor.yaml` rewrites for no reader benefit. Defer option C (a "by-domain" view inside `docs/skills/index.md`) until 2+ hubs exist.

1	# Browser automation skills & MCPs
2	
3	This page compares the popular **browser automation tools shipped as
4	agent skills or MCP servers**. Browser automation is one of the highest-
5	value capabilities you can give a coding agent — but the design choices
6	across these tools differ substantially. This page records the trade-offs
7	so the choice is explicit, and explains why this repo currently does
8	*not* vendor any of them.
9	
10	## At a glance
11	
12	Five well-known options, all roughly the same goal — let an agent open a
13	real browser and interact with pages — but very different shapes:
14	
15	| Tool | ⭐ | Form | Auth/session | Cost model | Token-efficient surface |
16	|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
17	| [`microsoft/playwright-cli`](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright-cli) | 10k | CLI + 1 SKILL.md | Local Chromium / your profile | Free, local | a11y-tree snapshot + `eN` refs |
18	| [`vercel-labs/agent-browser`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-browser) | 33k | CLI + 1 SKILL.md | Local Chromium, profile, Vercel Sandbox, AWS Bedrock AgentCore cloud | Free CLI; Vercel/AWS pay-as-you-go for cloud | a11y-tree snapshot + compact `@eN` refs |
19	| [`browser-use/browser-use`](https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use) | 93k | CLI + 4 SKILL.md (`browser-use`, `cloud`, `open-source`, `remote-browser`) | Local + Browser Use Cloud | Open-source local; Cloud SaaS | Persistent daemon (~50 ms/call); MCP also available |
20	| [`browserbase/stagehand`](https://github.com/browserbase/stagehand) | 23k | TypeScript SDK | Browserbase cloud (or local Playwright) | Browserbase metered | Code-first (`page.act("click sign in")`); not a SKILL.md |
21	| [Playwright MCP](https://playwright.dev/agent-cli/introduction) | (part of Playwright) | MCP server | Local Chromium | Free, local | a11y tree, but full MCP schema overhead |
22	
23	> Star counts are repo totals (the project, not just the skill). Don't
24	> use them to compare per-skill quality — `browser-use/browser-use` is a
25	> framework with very high stars; the SKILL.md inside it is one
26	> deliverable among many.
27	
28	## The design axes that actually matter
29	
30	Pick on these, not on stars:
31	
32	### 1. CLI vs MCP vs SDK
33	
34	- **CLI + SKILL.md** — `playwright-cli`, `agent-browser`, `browser-use`
35	  (CLI mode). The agent shells out to `playwright-cli click e15`. Each
36	  command is one short tool call; no MCP schema to load. **Best for
37	  token efficiency** when the agent has Bash access. The Microsoft
38	  README and the agent-browser README both argue this beats the MCP
39	  approach for high-throughput agent loops.
40	- **MCP server** — Playwright MCP, `browser-use` MCP. The agent calls
41	  `mcp_call("playwright.click", {...})`. Loads the full schema once;
42	  cleaner for agents without Bash but pays the MCP overhead. Token cost
43	  per call is higher than CLI for the same operation.
44	- **SDK** — Stagehand. You write TypeScript that calls `page.act("…")`.
45	  Powerful for *application code* you ship; not a skill the agent
46	  invokes ad-hoc.
47	
48	### 2. Snapshot strategy — a11y tree vs DOM vs vision
49	
50	- **Accessibility-tree snapshot + element refs** (`playwright-cli`,
51	  `agent-browser`, Playwright MCP). The agent sees a structured tree
52	  with stable `eN` / `@eN` refs and uses them directly. Token-cheap,
53	  reliable, no fragile selectors.
54	- **DOM + selectors** (older Playwright / Selenium patterns). Larger
55	  context, brittle.
56	- **Vision-first** (`magnitudedev/browser-agent`, 4k⭐). Agent reasons
57	  over screenshots. Robust against DOM changes; high token + latency
58	  cost; useful when the page is an opaque webapp.
59	
60	### 3. Where the browser actually runs
